fichas.title: Ventilation systems: purposes and construction
fichas.summary: Ventilation influences air cleanliness and odour, room air temperature, air movement and draughts, and humidity. A typical system comprises an outside-air intake with fan, central processing device, distribution ductwork and outlets. Systems are categorized by whether they supply outside air and by their air-processing functions; closed ventilation systems use no outside air. Illustrations show negative-pressure ventilation and air supply-and-extract systems.
uses: Provide ventilation and influence indoor air comfort
Transport and, where required, filter or process air

fichas.title: Chilled ceilings and related cooling systems
fichas.summary: Chilled ceilings provide passive radiant cooling using cold-water ceiling components, allowing air exchange to remain at the hygienic minimum. The page illustrates thin-construction chilled ceilings, suspended-ceiling cooling systems with a convection component, suspended and directly plastered ceiling arrangements, storage chilled ceilings, chilled beams, and cooling systems combined with suspended ceilings. Chilled ceilings are described as a quiet alternative to conventional air conditioning, with low space requirements for ducts and service rooms. Suspended chilled beams have less cooling capacity than full-surface systems.
spaces: Rooms served by chilled ceilings or chilled beams
uses: Remove internal cooling loads from people, devices and lighting
Combine cooling with ventilation and suspended-ceiling systems
